Prepare for a wall of text. There will be no TLDR except for this : The game isn't dead. It's simply taking a long time to release because of the current scope of the game. If you want a game made quickly with cut features, check out Destiny.

Other than that, here we go.

First, a little background. Chris Roberts made games like Wing Commander and Freelancer. While there were earlier space-sim games, CR made them popular. They were well made, pretty, and immersive games for their day. However, while making Freelancer, CR didn't get to do everything he wanted to do due to Microsoft Studios coming in and saying he was taking too long. The guy is a bit of a perfectionist. He then spent around a decade making movies in Hollywood before returning to the scene.

Now, about the game itself. Star Citizen is meant to be his magnum opus. The game he dreamed of making back in the turn of the millennium but was unable to do. Originally, the graphics and physics were toned down and the scope was smaller. However, the Kickstarter allowed them the option to incorporate more features as they reached their goal. What wasn't anticipated was the fact that everyone who had grown up with Wing Commander and Freelancer had been waiting for this type of game for most of their lives. It also helped that all of those people were now in their 30s and had actual jobs and decent money. Hence, the great Virtual Money Faucet of the 21st Century. Money was essentially thrown through the monitors into their accounts and they quickly exceeded their original goal. While it is debatable about the scope of the game and how achievable it is (google Derek Smart), the current situation was amplified by the fact that individuals with money wanted this game.

Okay, so here we are in 2015. The game changed around the end of last year when the company making the game, Cloud Imperium Games, decided to delay the release of the first module, Arena Commander, in order to implement something called Physics Based Rendering. This was a widely controversial move which drew a lot of hate from people because it was seen as a move away from the original scope which people backed. Most backers were content to wait because they were aware of CRs background in regard to this type of game. He was/is a perfectionist and this was the game he had been waiting to make for 10+ years. People who were not part of development or who had ulterior motives (again, see Derek Smart) were very hostile in regard to this design choice. Gamers, being what they are, were upset that the game was being delayed to incorporate more features. I always felt this was silly considering people were upset that Destiny took so long and delivered so little. Opinion-wise, I think it was the right move to make. It would be silly, IMHO, to continue with the original scope of the game considering they had made an excessive amount of money in such a short period. I mean, if you end up with too much money and produce a weak product, people would obviously get angry. Instead, CR decided to push the extra funds into hiring other studios to assist with development.

The previous sentence actually leads into my next topic of discussion. What many people do not realize is that CIG isn't doing all of the work. Several companies have been employed to work on Star Citizen. Illfonics, an FPS company, has been handling the FPS aspect of the game. The game itself uses a heavily modified CryEngine, which is the engine that Illfonics is most familiar with. Foundry 42, the German based section of CIG, works exclusively on the ships and the singleplayer component of the game. Kythera AI has been handling the advanced AI requirements for the game. The current aim of the game requires that around 10% of the avatars in-game will be players while the rest will be AI. This obviously requires a lot of different AI coding and it made sense to hire them to work through this mountain of work. In addition to a few of these companies (I think I missed one or two) there are two or three more CIG locations which handle specific aspects of the game development. The Austin, TX location is handling Persistent Universe development (the "MMO" aspect of the multiplayer component).

Now that I've talked about the background of the game and outlining most of its development, let's get into the nitty gritty. Why are they still accepting money? Well, this is America. When you discover a virtual money faucet, it is a silly decision to turn it off, especially when it is allowing you to continue development of your ambitious title. Keep in mind, CIG was originally going to seek investors to help with the costs if things got rocky. Those investors are no longer needed because the game is completely funded by private backers. The fact that they continue to sell virtual starships is a move which many people find odd and greedy. I suppose this is debatable depending on if you are a backer or not. For backers, it makes sense to us because we believe in the game and its lofty goals. Many backers have voiced a distaste for the current state of gaming due to lack of features in popular games and are tired of getting games before they are "fully developed". Many backers also put money into a similar title called Elite Dangerous and were a little saddened when the game was released and lacked some of the features they said would be in the game. Essentially, people felt that the game was a swimming pool a mile long but only a foot deep. A lot of people seemed to want a mile long swimming pool which was also a mile deep. These are the types of people who are backing Star Citizen. It's not the best example but I've still got some things to say on this.

This will be continued in a moment. Apparently walls of text cause Voat to think you're "doing that too fast". I've been "doing that too fast" for 30 minutes now.

Feature Creep. I hear this phrase thrown around more than any other in regards to Star Citizen. What is feature creep, exactly? Well, in my view, it is when a game is released and additional features are added in after development. Given Star Citizens transparent nature of development, many people feel the feature creep is a current problem while the game itself is still in development. This doesn't make a lot of sense to me, honestly, because the game, while taking a long time to develop, is trying to fulfill all of the promises made. Yes, the FPS aspect of the game was delayed. However, it was delayed because of a design and technological decision. As Star Citizen is planned to have FPS as a major aspect of the game, Chris Roberts felt that the release of the FPS module had to be as perfect as it could be. When Arena Commander (the dogfighting module) was released with some problems, it was decided that they wouldn't fall into the same pitfall twice. In addition, FPS is a popular genre of gaming and has been for quite some time. People have certain expectations, especially considering the game is technically the first AAA indie game. As such, the FPS module was delayed in order to revamp netcode backbone (netcode has been an issue since the launch of Arena Commander), refine and polish the FPS module, and generally work in features that CIG was excited about achieving (animation sync). Take this for what you want. I'm not here to push an agenda. While I am opinionated on the topic of SC, I feel delaying the FPS module was the right move given the current state of affairs regarding FPS in modern gaming. In addition, I felt the netcode was an issue which desperately needed a long hard look.

To continue, let's look at some of the feature creep that is anticipated. Fully explorable planets, a thriving in-game economy based upon player and AI choices, modular ships, over 100 star systems, ship boarding, and a few others which slip my mind. Most of the things I've listed here are currently slated for launch. Things like Fully explorable planets is something that they have stated will NOT be in the game at launch but they want to try and work it in. Obviously, that is a monumental task with 100 planned star systems at launch. Speaking of which, during a questionaire with devs, they stated that designing this many systems is possible before launch but it does mean a lot of work. They plan to work past this and include more star systems after launch which makes sense because it would be silly to stop adding content to a popular game after it launched. Just my 2 cents on that, really. The ships mentioned in the funding page will also be available at launch. Currently, they have claimed to have a developmental pipeline which allows them to work through ship design much faster than they used to. This means that the ships they're selling will be available at launch. It make take a while to get to launch but the content is promised to be there. Ship boarding is an aspect of the FPS module and is definitely going to be available prior to launch in the form of Arena Commander 2.0. Modular ships are already here, according to CIG, but the process for modding them is not. The modular ship aspect was created when they were developing the pipeline for ship creation. Since we can't utilize this feature, I have no real proof. Take that how you will, I guess. Overall, most features promised will be in the game prior to launch. So, in my view, the feature creep isn't a great description of the problem. The problem is the game will take a long ass time to develop but that's why they have delegated the work to other studios or designated some parts of CIG to only work on specific sections of the game.

So. Here we are. 2015 and the game was technically slated to have come out by now in some form or another. Chris Roberts promised quite a lot and thus far has taken this chance to improve on his original pitch to make the game he dreamed of 10+ years ago. I never got to achieve my dream and many of my friends didn't either. For many backers, this is a chance to show the gaming world that it IS possible to create a masterpiece in this day and age and it is possible to do so without the influence of publishers. Keep in mind, publishers are folks like EA Games, Ubisoft, Activision, and others. These are the guys that make a business decision to cut features in order to release a game in a timely manner and then scoop up money based off of the hype. Anyone remember Watch Dogs? Destiny? SimCity? All disappointing experiences with features that had been stripped. People flamed those companies because of their choices. Now, here we have a company which actually wants to deliver the promised features and may have the ability to do so and gamers are taking delight in flaming them for trying. In some ways, I feel this is a hypocritical view by your average gamer. You don't want feature creep but at the same time you don't want a game released too early? Every game is different and there is no Goldilocks zone of development. Personally, I do not feel the game will be vaporware. I have my reasons for this belief. Maybe it is because I am constantly following the development updates and I tirelessly follow dev posts in the forums. Maybe it's because I loved Chris Roberts games as a teenager and I believe in his dream of a perfect space-sim with trading, exploration, and a distinct lack of pay-to-win. Maybe it's because I'm a sucker with some money to spend. Frankly, I don't care what you want to call it. I believe in this project. I believe in Chris Roberts.

BONUS TIME! Ha ha, I almost forgot the biggest gripe of them all. The price of the ships, the continual accusations of "pay-to-win", and the fact that they keep releasing ships which seem to be overkill. I have a Constellation and a Vanguard. The first is a 4 man vessel while the second is a 2 man vessel. Both are slated to be combat oriented for the most part (although the Connie does fit multiple roles). I have dumped over $1k into the game thus far by buying these ships, going to the game convention, and subscribing to the monthly e-zine, Jump Point. Now, your average gamer will look at that and think "Well, this guy has just paid to win for sure!" As an owner of these ships, however, I am faced with the task of making money in-game in order to run these ships. I have to obtain a dedicated crew to run these ships with me and who won't mutiny. I will also have to deal with combat situations which may end up costing me more in-game currency than I make off of the battle itself. Compare this to the lowest cost entry into the game, a package which features an Aurora. The Aurora is a single seat ship which is best described either as a "flying coffin" or a "space minivan". It's much cheaper than either of my ships and does a lot less. In my view, it is compared to buying a minivan compared to buying a mobile RV fitted with 40 missiles. Obviously, the missile RV is going to cost a crap load more. Another thing to keep in mind is that EVERY SHIP IS OBTAINABLE IN-GAME. You will be able to start off with the $45 package, get into persistent universe, and work your way up. Maybe do mining or trade runs with your Aurora until you can get a shipping hauler, or a mining platform. From there, you make your cash until you buy another ship and hire a buddy to run that for you. 12 months from that point, you may be running your own industrial organization with 200+ employees. It's up to you. It's very similar to EVE in this aspect because combat isn't the end-all-be-all of Star Citizen. Getting rich and famous is, if you want. Maybe you want to get a frigate but don't want to pay $1k plus for it now. Fair enough. Earn it in-game and then hire the 10+ crew members to run it with you. Maybe you want to find the in-game Carrier, which is not purchasable, and then repair it for your own use. That can be done too but keep in mind that ship requires 700+ people to fully staff. In addition, once the game launches, it has been promised that ships will NOT be purchasable with real money. Once the game launches, you can't simply buy your way to the top. The only confirmed microtransactions has been stated as being: character slots and in-game currency. The in-game currency has a monthly cap. You won't even be able to buy your way to riches. You'll have to actually play the game.

Anyway, I didn't expect to write this wall of text and have likely missed something. I'm not going to be up all night answering questions but I'll do my best. I have followed this game since its conception and I know many details that have been released. While many news articles poke fun at this game and call it a scam, I can assure you it is not. Ambitious, yes. Scam, not at all. If it was a scam, CR would already be on his private island and would be giving the finger to everyone. I have also heard that if he stays in a major country in the event of "take the money and run", then he will be dragged out into the street and lynched by many of the backers who have spent well over $10k on the game.
It seems like it continues being developed and updated. People are just freaking over some normal delay.

Star citizen looks amazing, and I really want it to happen, but everything points to it being a highly calculated money generating machine, not a great game.

Why do they have playing cards, baseball caps, ship models, useless digital ships, and fake money for sale when they do not yet have a completed game? This shows that they are milking the hype for as much as possible, focusing on making money rather than making a game. Why spend time, money, and effort on a youtube update show when they could be working on the game? Because they know that fanboys will spend the money on it and they know that money will keep coming as long as they have a carrot that they can dangle in front of people.

This does not bode well for the game itself supposing it ever does get completed. This focus on money generation make is fairly easy to assume that they will have payed DLC and the game will essentially be pay to win, because again their target is fanboys with large amounts of expendable income.

I wanted so badly to buy a ship and play arena commander, but I don't want to get too hyped about a game that will be pay to win and who knows when it will come out.
Essentially, the game has received dozens of millions in funding, has been in development for like 4 years and all it has to show so far is essentially a glorified tech demo.
I would step back and give Star Citizen a chance. Even with the very long development cycle. I am willing to bet, and I have (base level supporter), that they are going to surprise people.
